LESSON: LABORATORY APPARATUS AND INSTRUMENTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Scientific Investigation
Topic 1.3: Laboratory apparatus and instruments
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Laboratory apparatus and instruments, part of Scientific Investigation in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven INTEGRATED SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why are basic skills in science important? 2. How are quantities in science expressed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Discuss in purposive pairs the meaning and use of basic skills in science and record findings. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views during discussion.

2. Practice use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory (for heating, measuring mass, temperature, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss in purposive pairs the meaning and use of basic skills in science and record findings. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views during discussion.
2. Practice use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory (for heating, measuring mass, temperature, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Laboratory apparatus and instruments together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: The learner practices use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.

● Communication and collaboration: The learner collaboratively carry out activities on measurements of basic quantities and

express them in the International System of Units.

Values:
● Respect: The learner work harmoniously with peers when carrying out activities to determine derived units from basic units

working.

● Responsibility: The learner learns how care for apparatus and instruments as they practise how to care and use them in the

laboratory.

9

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Socio economic issues: The learner links the quantity of goods parked to their prices as they collects packaging with labels of

quantities and discuss the importance of the information on labels.

Link to other learning areas:

• The learner is able to link the packaging of goods and labels of quantities form inputs and product labels learnt in Agriculture

and Nutrition.

• The learner uses mathematical manipulation skills in recording and working measurements.
